LESSON: RHYTHM

Grade: SNE  /  physical-impairment / Grade one
Subject: CREATIVE ACTIVITIES
Strand: Creating and Execution
Topic 1.6: Rhythm
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 14

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Rhythm, part of Creating and Execution in SNE  /  physical-impairment / Grade one CREATIVE ACTIVITIES.

Key inquiry question: How can different body percussion be used to accompany songs?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

A. identify body percussion that accompany singing,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Rhythm in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

B. use body percussion to maintain the beat while singing simple songs, ● Learners to watch live or recorded performances with body percussion accompaniments and identify them. Learners with postural defects or short stature could be appropriately positioned for comfort and clear view. Screen resolution and light intensity How can different body percussion be used to accompany songs? 18 ● Body movement: walking, jumping, skipping, leaping

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Rhythm in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

C. create rhythmic accompaniments to simple songs using body percussion,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Rhythm in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

D. make body movements in line patterns to maintain rhythm,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Rhythm in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

E. appreciate the use of body percussion in creating rhythm. could be regulated for learners who are sensitive to light. ● Learners to collaborative practise performing various body percussion to maintain beat. ● Learners to use body percussion to accompany familiar topical songs. Learners with manipulation difficulties could use alternative functional parts of the body or use assistive technology. ● Learners to take turns to sing songs accompanied with body percussion to maintain rhythm. Learners with speech difficulties could use residual speech, hum, mime or use alternative mode of communications. ● Learners to perform body movements in different line patterns accompanied with body percussion to maintain rhythm. Learners with postural defects could use alternative functional parts of the body, perform an 19 alternative corresponding activity, or perform at their level of functional ability. ● Learners to improvise body percussion accompaniments to the songs sung and record them using a digital device. Learners with manipulation difficulties could use alternative functional parts of the body, use adapted digital devices, assistive technology or be supported. ● Learners to play the recorded performance and give feedback.

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

Follow your teacher’s guidance for group work, discussion, and practice on this topic.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Rhythm together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
● Creativity and Imagination: as the learner uses and explores their parts of the body to create rhythmic accompaniments to

various songs.

● Learning to learn: as the learner learns new ways to use body movements to maintain the beat outside the class alone or

with others.

● Digital literacy: as the learner interacts with a digital device to record the improvised body percussion accompaniments to

the songs sung.

Values:
● Social Justice is promoted as the learner improvises rhythmic accompaniment using body percussion to songs from diverse

Kenyan communities developing a sense of diverse cultural awareness.

● Responsibility is promoted as the learner sings songs and takes turns to accompany others with body percussion to

maintain rhythm.
